observations: The component itself renders no images or icons. `content`/`content-top`/`content-bottom` are trusted HTML rendered via `unsafeHTML`; if an implementer embeds an `` in any of them, compliance for that image's alt text is the implementer's responsibility, same as `ct-paragraph`/`ct-table`.

standard: 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (Level A)

observations: The trigger-to-panel relationship is established programmatically by the component itself, not left to the implementer: the panel gets role="dialog" and an id, and the trigger gets aria-haspopup="dialog"/aria-expanded/aria-controls pointing at that id (via the Zag.js popover machine's connect() output, forwarded onto ct-link's real anchor through its new ARIA-passthrough properties - see popover.ts's doc comment). No manual id/aria wiring is required from the implementer.
The component is a disclosure trigger and content panel, not a form input; it collects no user data.
The panel's presence is conveyed through the hidden attribute/positioning and the trigger's own aria-expanded state, not through color alone.

Both themes were verified against civictheme.variables.css-sourced tokens: light theme is #33444a text (--ct-color-light-body) on a #fdfdfd panel background (--ct-popover-light-content-background-color, aliasing --ct-color-light-background-light) - approximately 9.9:1. Dark theme is #e7f9ff text (--ct-color-dark-body) on a #003a4f panel background (--ct-popover-dark-content-background-color, aliasing --ct-color-dark-background) - approximately 11.3:1. Both comfortably exceed 4.5:1. The trigger link's own contrast is `ct-link`'s existing, separately-verified concern.
The panel has a min-width/min-height (not a fixed width/height) and no overflow:hidden clipping, so it grows with content at 200% zoom rather than truncating it.
The component renders no images of text itself; compliance depends on the implementer not embedding an image-of-text into `content`/`content-top`/`content-bottom`.

The panel has a min-width (--ct-popover-min-width, 17.5rem) but no max-width, so it grows to fit its content without an upper bound; compliance for very wide embedded `content` (e.g. a wide unbroken table) depends on the implementer keeping embedded markup reasonably responsive, same caveat as `ct-paragraph`.

The trigger's :focus-visible outline is `ct-link`'s own, already-verified token-driven outline (--ct-outline-width/--ct-outline-light/--ct-outline-dark), reused unmodified since the trigger is a real composed `ct-link` rather than a reimplementation.
No fixed-height container clips panel content when line/letter/word spacing is increased per the criterion's multipliers.

standard: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA)
observations: Unlike ct-tooltip, this component is click-triggered only (aria-haspopup="dialog" plus a real click/Enter activation) - the panel never appears merely as a side effect of hover or focus, so 1.4.13's hover/focus-triggered-content requirements do not apply. This is a deliberate divergence from ct-tooltip's interaction model, matching upstream popover.twig's click-based `data-collapsible` behavior rather than tooltip.twig's hover/focus behavior.

The trigger is a real, composed ct-link anchor, reachable via Tab and operable via Enter (native anchor activation) or a mouse/pointer click. Space does not activate it, since it is rendered as an anchor rather than a native button - this matches upstream, which also renders the trigger as a civictheme:link anchor rather than a button, so it is not a regression introduced by this port.

Focus moves into the panel on open (Zag's autoFocus) and back to the trigger on close (restoreFocus), both defaults of the Zag.js popover machine; nothing traps focus inside the panel - Tab can move past it normally.
No single-character key shortcuts are implemented.
The panel has no auto-dismiss timer of any kind; it stays open until explicitly closed.

standard: 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (Level A)

observations: Focus order follows DOM order (trigger, then panel content when open); the component does not manipulate tabindex beyond the panel's own tabIndex=-1 fallback focus target.

Unlike ct-tooltip (an icon-only button trigger), this component's trigger IS a link, so this criterion genuinely applies: compliance depends on the implementer providing a descriptive `trigger-text` (e.g. "What is CivicTheme?", not "Click here" or "More").

Compliance depends on the implementer providing `trigger-text` (and `content`) that clearly describes what the panel will disclose. `trigger-text` renders as plain link text, not a `<label>`/`<legend>` element, so the mechanical rules.mjs 2.4.6 extractor (label/legend text only) does not apply to it - the same structural gap noted for ct-heading/ct-tooltip.
The trigger reuses ct-link's own :focus-visible outline unmodified, already verified in both themes.
The panel is positioned by the floating-ui-based Zag machine with a `flip` fallback (bottom-start placement) so it does not render on top of the trigger that opened it.
Only a simple pointer click is used; no multipoint or path-based gesture.
Opening/closing fires on click completion (onClick), not on an unabortable pointerdown; the trigger's onPointerDown handler only re-focuses the element on Safari and does not itself toggle the panel.

ct-popover exposes no aria-label override of its own for the trigger, so the trigger's accessible name is always exactly its visible `trigger-text` - there is no way through this component's public API to set a mismatching accessible name.

The trigger renders as ordinary inline link text (not an icon-only control), which WCAG 2.5.8 explicitly exempts as an inline exception; compliance for a non-exempt layout (e.g. a very short single-character `trigger-text` presented in isolation rather than within a sentence) depends on the implementer's surrounding context.
The document's lang attribute is outside this component's scope.
Compliance depends on the implementer setting a lang attribute on `trigger-text`/`content` if their language differs from the surrounding page.
Focusing the trigger alone does not open the panel - only an explicit click or Enter activation does - so no unexpected change of context occurs purely as a result of focus.
The component has no input controls of its own; opening the panel is a direct, expected result of activating the trigger, not an unexpected side effect.
Compliance depends on the implementer using the same `trigger-text` wording (and `group`, where relevant) for popovers serving the same purpose across a site.
The component has no form-validation role.
The component is not a form input.

The Zag.js machine provides role/state wiring automatically (role="dialog" on the panel, aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls on the trigger via ct-link's new ARIA passthrough, data-state reflecting open/closed) - but the trigger's own accessible Name still depends on the implementer supplying a non-empty `trigger-text`; `triggerText` is required in PopoverSchema, but the Lit component does not enforce a non-empty value at runtime (same caveat as ct-tooltip's `label` and ct-label's `content`).
The panel opening is a direct result of the user's own click/Enter activation of a visible control, not an out-of-band status update requiring an aria-live region.
